nodes.label: Inorganic Chemistry
nodes.note: Complete JEE Main inorganic roadmap: periodicity, s/p/d/f blocks, hydrogen, bonding, equilibrium, redox, electrochemistry, coordination compounds, metallurgy, qualitative analysis and environmental chemistry. Nodes group every pillar chapter, its core trends and the named tests/reagents asked in PYQs.

nodes.label: Periodic Table and Periodicity
nodes.note: Pillar chapter: Periodic Table and Periodicity. Collects its JEE Main subtopics, trends and named tests in one branch.

nodes.label: Electronic Configuration and Blocks
nodes.note: Every element's block is fixed by its valence subshell: $$ns^{1-2}$$ is s-block, $$ns^2np^{1-6}$$ is p-block, $$(n-1)d^{1-10}ns^{0-2}$$ is d-block, and $$(n-2)f^{0-14}$$ is f-block. Expect questions on which orbital holds the differentiating electron.

nodes.label: Atomic and Ionic Radius
nodes.note: Radius decreases across a period (rising $$Z_{eff}$$) and increases down a group. Cations shrink: $$Na^+ < Na$$; anions expand: $$Cl^- > Cl$$. Isoelectronic size order: $$N^{3-} > O^{2-} > F^- > Na^+ > Mg^{2+} > Al^{3+}$$.

nodes.label: Ionisation Enthalpy
nodes.note: Energy to remove the most loosely held electron: $$M(g) \rightarrow M^+(g) + e^-$$. IE rises across a period and falls down a group; successive IEs $$IE_1 < IE_2 < IE_3$$ jump when a noble-gas core is broken.

nodes.label: IE Exceptions (N>O, Be>B, Mg>Al)
nodes.note: Half-filled and fully-filled subshells are extra stable, so $$N > O$$ (N has $$2p^3$$) and $$Be > B$$, $$Mg > Al$$. A JEE classic trap: although IE generally increases across a period, these two dips recur every period.

nodes.label: Electron Gain Enthalpy
nodes.note: Energy change on adding an electron: $$X(g) + e^- \rightarrow X^-(g)$$. It usually becomes more negative across a period, but Cl has the most negative EGE, not F, because tiny $$F^-$$ suffers lone-pair repulsion.

nodes.label: Electronegativity
nodes.note: Pauling's scale measures an atom's electron-pulling power; F (4.0) is the maximum and decreases down a group and increases across a period. It predicts bond polarity and whether a hydride is ionic or covalent.

nodes.label: Metallic and Non-metallic Character
nodes.note: Metallic character (ease of losing electrons) increases down a group and decreases across a period, opposite to non-metallic character. Highest metallic: Fr/Cs; highest non-metallic: F.

nodes.label: Periodicity of Oxidation States
nodes.note: Maximum oxidation state often equals the group number through $$+7$$, then falls after Mn: $$Cr^{+6}$$, $$Mn^{+7}$$ in $$KMnO_4$$, $$Fe^{+6}$$ in $$K_2FeO_4$$. Lower states stabilise down a group (inert pair effect, later).

nodes.label: S Block Elements
nodes.note: Pillar chapter: S Block Elements. Collects its JEE Main subtopics, trends and named tests in one branch.

nodes.label: Group 1: Alkali Metals
nodes.note: Soft, low-melting metals with configuration $$ns^1$$: Li, Na, K, Rb, Cs, Fr. Very low IE makes them powerful reducing agents; hydration enthalpy of $$Li^+$$ is the largest in the group.

nodes.label: Oxides, Peroxides, Superoxides
nodes.note: Combustion in air gives oxides (Li: $$Li_2O$$), peroxides (Na: $$Na_2O_2$$) and superoxides (K, Rb, Cs: $$KO_2$$). Superoxides like $$KO_2$$ liberate $$O_2$$, used in submarine air supply: $$4KO_2 + 2CO_2 \rightarrow 2K_2CO_3 + 3O_2$$.

nodes.label: Solution in Liquid NH3 (Blue)
nodes.note: Dissolved alkali metals give a deep blue paramagnetic solution from solvated electrons: $$M + (x+y)NH_3 \rightarrow [M(NH_3)_x]^+ + [e(NH_3)_y]^-$$. On standing it decomposes to $$NaNH_2$$ plus $$H_2$$.

nodes.label: Group 2: Alkaline Earth Metals
nodes.note: Harder, denser metals $$ns^2$$: Be, Mg, Ca, Sr, Ba, Ra. Solubility of hydroxides rises down the group while solubility of sulfates falls: $$BeSO_4, MgSO_4$$ soluble, $$BaSO_4$$ insoluble.

nodes.label: Anomalous Be and Mg
nodes.note: Small Be shows covalent character: $$BeCl_2$$ is polymeric and $$BeCO_3$$ is unstable; Mg forms a nitride $$Mg_3N_2$$ unlike other group members and its carbonate decomposes most easily. These are fixed JEE favourites.

nodes.label: Diagonal Relationship (Li-Mg, Be-Al)
nodes.note: Li resembles Mg and Be resembles Al: similar polarising power gives amphoteric hydroxides, covalent chlorides and nitride formation. Example: both Li and Mg form nitrides, $$Li_3N$$ and $$Mg_3N_2$$, on heating in air.

nodes.label: Flame Test Colors (s-Block)
nodes.note: Characteristic flame emission: Li crimson red, Na golden yellow, K lilac (violet), Ca brick red, Sr crimson red, Ba apple green. Be and Mg show no characteristic flame since their excitation energies lie in the UV.

nodes.label: Thermal Stability of Carbonates and Nitrates
nodes.note: Stability of carbonates and nitrates increases down a group because the larger cation polarises the anion less: $$MCO_3 \rightarrow MO + CO_2$$, $$2MNO_3 \rightarrow 2MNO_2 + O_2$$. $$Li_2CO_3$$ and $$LiNO_3$$ decompose most easily in Group 1.

nodes.label: Important Sodium Compounds
nodes.note: NaOH (caustic soda, Castner-Kellner cell), $$Na_2CO_3$$ (washing soda, Solvay process) and $$NaHCO_3$$ (baking soda, mild) dominate JEE. $$Na_2CO_3$$ on heating does not decompose (unlike $$Li_2CO_3$$).

nodes.label: Solvay Process for Na2CO3
nodes.note: Industrial preparation: $$NaCl + NH_3 + CO_2 + H_2O \rightarrow NaHCO_3 + NH_4Cl$$, then $$2NaHCO_3 \xrightarrow{\Delta} Na_2CO_3 + CO_2 + H_2O$$. Note $$K_2CO_3$$ cannot be made this way because $$KHCO_3$$ is too soluble.

nodes.label: Important Calcium Compounds
nodes.note: Key substances: quicklime $$CaO$$, slaked lime $$Ca(OH)_2$$, lime water, bleaching powder $$CaOCl_2$$, and plaster of Paris $$CaSO_4 \cdot \tfrac{1}{2}H_2O$$. Setting of POP is crystallisation of gypsum: $$CaSO_4 \cdot \tfrac{1}{2}H_2O + \tfrac{3}{2}H_2O \rightarrow CaSO_4 \cdot 2H_2O$$.

nodes.label: P Block Elements
nodes.note: Pillar chapter: P Block Elements. Collects its JEE Main subtopics, trends and named tests in one branch.

nodes.label: Group 13: Boron Family
nodes.note: Boron is a metalloid with electron-deficient $$BCl_3$$; Al is amphoteric: $$Al_2O_3 + 2NaOH \rightarrow 2NaAlO_2 + H_2O$$. Gallium, indium and thallium show increasing inert-pair stability of the $$+1$$ state down the group.

nodes.label: Group 14: Carbon Family
nodes.note: C, Si, Ge, Sn, Pb with states $$+4$$ and $$+2$$; stability of $$+2$$ grows down the group (inert pair effect). $$CO_2$$ is a gas while $$SiO_2$$ is a giant covalent solid; watch oxidation states: $$PbO_2$$ is a strong oxidiser, $$PbCl_4$$ unstable.

nodes.label: Group 15: Nitrogen Family
nodes.note: N, P, As, Sb, Bi. Nitrogen shows $$p\pi-p\pi$$ back-bonding ($$N_2$$, $$N_2O$$, NO) unlike heavier congeners. $$NH_3$$ is basic, $$HNO_3$$ is a strong oxidising acid, and $$PCl_5$$ exists while $$NCl_5$$ does not (no d-orbitals).

nodes.label: Haber Process for Ammonia
nodes.note: Industrial synthesis: $$N_2(g) + 3H_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2NH_3(g)$$, exothermic, favoured by high pressure ~200 atm and Fe catalyst with Mo promoter. A high-pressure, moderately heated equilibrium compromise.

nodes.label: Oxoacids of Nitrogen
nodes.note: Key acids: $$HNO_2$$ (nitrous, unstable), $$HNO_3$$ (nitric), $$H_2N_2O_2$$ (hyponitrous). Basicity = number of $$-OH$$ groups; $$H_3PO_2$$ and $$H_3PO_3$$ are reducing, $$HNO_3$$ oxidising.

nodes.label: Group 16: Oxygen Family
nodes.note: O, S, Se, Te, Po. $$O_3$$ (ozone) is a bent triatomic allotrope: $$2O_3 \rightarrow 3O_2$$. Sulfur's acids dominate: $$H_2SO_4$$ (contact process, strong dehydrating agent) and $$H_2S_2O_8$$ (peroxodisulfuric, has $$-O-O-$$ linkage).

nodes.label: Contact Process for H2SO4
nodes.note: Sulfur burned to $$SO_2$$, catalytically oxidised: $$2SO_2 + O_2 \rightleftharpoons[V_2O_5]{} 2SO_3$$, then absorbed in $$H_2SO_4$$ to give oleum $$H_2S_2O_7$$, diluted to $$H_2SO_4$$.

nodes.label: Ozone Layer Chemistry
nodes.note: CFCs release Cl radicals that destroy ozone: $$Cl + O_3 \rightarrow ClO + O_2$$, $$ClO + O \rightarrow Cl + O_2$$. This radical chain thins the stratospheric ozone layer, increasing harmful UV-B at the surface.

nodes.label: Group 17: Halogens
nodes.note: F, Cl, Br, I with configuration $$ns^2np^5$$. Bond dissociation anomaly: $$F_2$$ has lower bond energy than $$Cl_2$$ due to lone-pair repulsion. All form $$HX$$; $$HF$$ is the weakest acid yet forms $$HF_2^-$$ ($$F^- \cdots HF$$).

nodes.label: Halogen Oxoacids
nodes.note: Order of acid strength $$HOCl < HClO_2 < HClO_3 < HClO_4$$; oxidising power decreases down the order. $$HClO_4$$ is the strongest halogen acid; perhalates are powerful oxidisers.

nodes.label: Group 18: Noble Gases
nodes.note: He, Ne, Ar, Kr, Xe, Rn with closed shells $$ns^2np^6$$ (He: $$1s^2$$). Only heavier noble gases form compounds: $$XeF_2$$ (linear), $$XeF_4$$ (square planar), $$XeO_3$$ (pyramidal) via VSEPR with lone pairs.

nodes.label: Xenon Fluorides (XeF2, XeF4, XeF6)
nodes.note: Direct fluorination: $$Xe + F_2 \xrightarrow{Ni, 673K} XeF_2$$, $$Xe + 2F_2 \xrightarrow{Ni, 873K} XeF_4$$, $$Xe + 3F_2 \xrightarrow{Ni, 1173K} XeF_6$$. Hydrolysis of $$XeF_6$$: $$XeF_6 + H_2O \rightarrow XeOF_4 + 2HF$$.

nodes.label: Inert Pair Effect
nodes.note: Down groups 13-15 the $$ns^2$$ pair resists bonding, stabilising lower oxidation states: $$Tl^+ > Tl^{3+}$$, $$Pb^{2+} > Pb^{4+}$$, $$Bi^{3+} > Bi^{5+}$$. A direct periodicity consequence examiners love.

nodes.label: Hydrogen
nodes.note: Pillar chapter: Hydrogen. Collects its JEE Main subtopics, trends and named tests in one branch.

nodes.label: Isotopes and Preparation of H2
nodes.note: Protium $$^1H$$, deuterium $$^2H$$ (D), radioactive tritium $$^3H$$. Lab preparation: $$Zn + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow ZnSO_4 + H_2$$; large scale via steam reforming: $$CH_4 + H_2O \xrightarrow{1273K} CO + 3H_2$$.

nodes.label: Water Gas Shift Reaction
nodes.note: To increase $$H_2$$ yield, CO in water gas is shifted: $$CO + H_2O \xrightarrow{673K} CO_2 + H_2$$. Iron-chrome or copper-zinc oxide catalysts are used industrially.

nodes.label: Types of Hydrides
nodes.note: Ionic (saline): $$NaH, CaH_2$$; covalent: $$CH_4, NH_3, H_2O, HF$$; interstitial (metallic): non-stoichiometric, e.g. $$PdH_{0.6}$$, electrically conducting. Trend in boiling points: $$H_2O$$ anomalously high due to H-bonding.

nodes.label: Hydrogen Peroxide (H2O2)
nodes.note: Prepared by anthraquinone process; structure has $$-O-O-$$ bridge: $$H-O-O-H$$ with dihedral angle ~109.8 deg in gas. $$H_2O_2$$ acts as both oxidiser and reducer: $$H_2O_2 + 2KI \rightarrow 2KOH + I_2$$, $$H_2O_2 + Ag_2O \rightarrow 2Ag + H_2O + O_2$$.

nodes.label: Structure and Bond Angle of H2O2
nodes.note: Open book (skewed) structure with O-O single bond; gas dihedral 111.5 deg, crystalline altered by H-bonding. Oxidation state of O is $$-1$$, between $$-2$$ (water) and $$0$$ ($$O_2$$).

nodes.label: Water and Heavy Water
nodes.note: $$H_2O$$ is a bent molecule ($$\angle H-O-H \approx 104.5^\circ$$) with strong H-bonding giving high boiling point. Heavy water $$D_2O$$ is used as a moderator in nuclear reactors and in NMR/tracer studies.

nodes.label: D and F Block Elements
nodes.note: Pillar chapter: D and F Block Elements. Collects its JEE Main subtopics, trends and named tests in one branch.

nodes.label: General Properties of d-Block
nodes.note: Transition metals show variable oxidation states, coloured ions, paramagnetism and catalytic activity. Config: $$(n-1)d^{1-10}ns^{1-2}$$ with the exception of $$Cr: [Ar]3d^54s^1$$ and $$Cu: [Ar]3d^{10}4s^1$$.

nodes.label: Oxidation States and Trends
nodes.note: Max oxidation state peaks at group 7: $$Mn^{+7}$$ in $$Mn_2O_7$$; $$Sc^{+3}$$ and $$Zn^{+2}$$ are common. High states are oxidising ($$Cr_2O_7^{2-}$$), low states often reducing ($$V^{2+}$$).

nodes.label: Spin-Only Magnetic Moment
nodes.note: For unpaired electrons n: $$\mu_{so} = \sqrt{n(n+2)}$$ BM. Used to count d-electrons, e.g. $$Fe^{3+}$$ (d5): $$\mu = \sqrt{5 \cdot 7} = 5.92$$ BM.

nodes.label: Lanthanoid Contraction
nodes.note: Poor shielding by 4f electrons shrinks radii across the lanthanoids: $$La^{3+}$$ (106 pm) to $$Lu^{3+}$$ (85 pm). Consequence: 4d and 5d pairs (Zr/Hf, Nb/Ta, Mo/W) have nearly equal radii and chemistry.

nodes.label: Important d-Block Compounds
nodes.note: $$KMnO_4$$ (purple, strong oxidiser), $$K_2Cr_2O_7$$ (orange, oxidiser in acid), $$K_2CrO_4$$ (yellow), and $$FeSO_4 \cdot (NH_4)_2SO_4 \cdot 6H_2O$$ (Mohr's salt). Colour: $$MnO_4^-$$ purple, $$CrO_4^{2-}$$ yellow, $$Cr_2O_7^{2-}$$ orange.

nodes.label: KMnO4 as Oxidant
nodes.note: In acid: $$MnO_4^- + 8H^+ + 5e^- \rightarrow Mn^{2+} + 4H_2O$$ (purple to colourless). In neutral/alkaline medium it reduces to $$MnO_2$$: $$MnO_4^- + 2H_2O + 3e^- \rightarrow MnO_2 + 4OH^-$$.

nodes.label: Cr2O7^2- / CrO4^2- Equilibrium
nodes.note: $$Cr_2O_7^{2-} + 2OH^- \rightleftharpoons 2CrO_4^{2-} + H_2O$$. Orange dichromate in acid, yellow chromate in base - classic Le Chatelier demo.

nodes.label: Transition Metal Catalysts
nodes.note: Fe (Haber, with Mo promoter), $$V_2O_5$$ (contact), Ni (hydrogenation), Pt/Pd (petroleum reforming). Adsorption of reactants on the surface and availability of d-orbitals explain activity.

nodes.label: F-Block: Lanthanoids and Actinoids
nodes.note: Lanthanoids (4f) are silvery, with common state $$+3$$; $$Ce^{4+}$$ and $$Eu^{2+}$$ are notable. Actinoids (5f) are radioactive, all show $$+3$$, and heavier ones have low stability; $$U^{6+}$$ in uranyl $$UO_2^{2+}$$.

nodes.label: Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure
nodes.note: Pillar chapter: Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure. Collects its JEE Main subtopics, trends and named tests in one branch.

nodes.label: Ionic Bond and Lattice Enthalpy
nodes.note: Formed by electron transfer giving a cation-anion lattice; lattice enthalpy is the energy released when gaseous ions form a solid, $$Na^+(g) + Cl^-(g) \rightarrow NaCl(s)$$. Higher charges and smaller ions give larger lattice enthalpy.

nodes.label: Born-Haber Cycle
nodes.note: Hess-law bookkeeping of formation: $$\Delta H_f = S + \tfrac{1}{2}D + IE + EA - U$$. Lets you estimate lattice energy or electron affinity that cannot be measured directly.

nodes.label: Covalent Bonding and VBT
nodes.note: VBT: bonds form by overlap of half-filled orbitals with paired spins ($$\sigma$$ by head-on, $$\pi$$ by sideways overlap). $$\sigma$$ is stronger than $$\pi$$; $$N_2$$'s triple bond $$N \equiv N$$ has one $$\sigma$$ and two $$\pi$$.

nodes.label: VSEPR Theory and Geometries
nodes.note: Geometry follows electron-pair repulsion: $$AX_2$$ linear, $$AX_3$$ trigonal planar, $$AX_4$$ tetrahedral, $$AX_2E_2$$ bent ($$H_2O$$, 104.5 deg), $$AX_3E$$ pyramidal ($$NH_3$$, 107 deg). Lone pairs compress bond angles.

nodes.label: Hybridization
nodes.note: Mixing of orbitals gives directed geometry: $$sp$$ (linear), $$sp^2$$ (trigonal planar), $$sp^3$$ (tetrahedral), $$dsp^2$$ (square planar), $$sp^3d^2$$ (octahedral). Count $$\sigma$$ bonds + lone pairs to assign.

nodes.label: Molecular Orbital Theory
nodes.note: MOs form by LCAO; for Z <= 7 the order is $$\sigma 1s < \sigma^*1s < \sigma 2s < \sigma^*2s < \pi 2p < \sigma 2p < \pi^*2p < \sigma^*2p$$, and for O, F, Ne the $$\sigma 2p$$ and $$\pi 2p$$ swap. Bond order $$BO = \tfrac{1}{2}(N_b - N_a)$$ sets stability: $$O_2$$ has BO = 2 and is paramagnetic.

nodes.label: Dipole Moment and Molecular Polarity
nodes.note: $$\mu = q \cdot d$$. $$CO_2$$ (linear, two opposing dipoles) has $$\mu = 0$$ though C=O is polar; $$H_2O$$ and $$NH_3$$ are polar. $$NF_3 < NH_3$$ in $$\mu$$ because lone-pair and bond dipoles oppose in $$NF_3$$.

nodes.label: Fajan's Rules of Polarization
nodes.note: Small highly charged cations and large polarisable anions increase covalent character: $$LiI$$ more covalent than $$LiF$$; $$AlCl_3$$ covalent, $$AlF_3$$ ionic. Explains solubility and colour trends.

nodes.label: Hydrogen Bonding
nodes.note: H covalently bound to F/O/N is attracted to a lone pair on F/O/N: $$O-H \cdots O$$. Explains high bp of $$H_2O, HF, NH_3$$ and why ice (open cage) floats: max density of water at 4 deg C.

nodes.label: Open Cage Structure of Ice
nodes.note: Each water in ice H-bonds tetrahedrally to four neighbours, leaving cavities; volume expands on freezing so ice is less dense (0.917 g/cm3) and floats. This is vital for aquatic life in winter.

nodes.label: Intermolecular Forces (vdW)
nodes.note: London dispersion (all molecules, rises with size), dipole-dipole, and H-bonding (strongest). Boiling points: $$He < Ar < Kr$$ from rising dispersion; polar $$HCl$$ boils above non-polar $$F_2$$ of similar mass.

nodes.label: Chemical and Ionic Equilibrium
nodes.note: Pillar chapter: Chemical and Ionic Equilibrium. Collects its JEE Main subtopics, trends and named tests in one branch.

nodes.label: Equilibrium Constant Kc and Kp
nodes.note: For $$aA + bB \rightleftharpoons cC + dD$$, $$K_c = \frac{[C]^c[D]^d}{[A]^a[B]^b}$$ and $$K_p = K_c(RT)^{\Delta n_g}$$. Solids and pure liquids are omitted. Large K means products dominate at equilibrium.

nodes.label: Le Chatelier's Principle
nodes.note: A system at equilibrium shifts to counter any imposed change. For $$N_2 + 3H_2 \rightleftharpoons 2NH_3$$ ($$\Delta H < 0$$), high pressure and low temperature favour $$NH_3$$; a catalyst only speeds attainment of equilibrium.

nodes.label: Degree of Dissociation
nodes.note: Fraction dissociated $$\alpha$$; for $$N_2O_4 \rightleftharpoons 2NO_2$$, $$K_p = \frac{4\alpha^2 P}{1-\alpha^2}$$. Higher temperature shifts toward more $$NO_2$$ (browner gas) since dissociation is endothermic.

nodes.label: Acids, Bases and pH
nodes.note: $$pH = -\log[H^+]$$, $$pOH = 14 - pH$$ at 25 deg C. Strong acid $$HCl$$: $$pH = -\log C$$; weak acid $$CH_3COOH$$: $$[H^+] = \sqrt{K_a C}$$. $$K_w = 10^{-14}$$ links $$K_a$$ and $$K_b$$: $$K_w = K_a K_b$$.

nodes.label: Buffer Solutions
nodes.note: A weak acid plus its conjugate base resists pH change; Henderson-Hasselbalch: $$pH = pK_a + \log\frac{[\text{salt}]}{[\text{acid}]}$$. Blood ($$H_2CO_3/HCO_3^-$$) is the classic biological buffer.

nodes.label: Salt Hydrolysis
nodes.note: Salts of weak acid + strong base give basic solutions ($$CH_3COONa$$, $$pH > 7$$): $$CH_3COO^- + H_2O \rightleftharpoons CH_3COOH + OH^-$$. Salt of strong acid + weak base gives $$pH < 7$$ ($$NH_4Cl$$); weak+weak depends on $$K_a$$ vs $$K_b$$.

nodes.label: Solubility Product Ksp
nodes.note: For $$MX_2(s) \rightleftharpoons M^{2+} + 2X^-$$, $$K_{sp} = [M^{2+}][X^-]^2 = 4s^3$$. Precipitation starts when ionic product $$Q > K_{sp}$$; common ion effect suppresses solubility - basis of Group I/II cation separation.

nodes.label: Redox Reactions
nodes.note: Pillar chapter: Redox Reactions. Collects its JEE Main subtopics, trends and named tests in one branch.

nodes.label: Oxidation Number Rules
nodes.note: Rules: free element 0, $$O$$ is $$-2$$ (except peroxides $$-1$$, $$OF_2$$ $$+2$$), $$H$$ is $$+1$$ (except hydrides $$-1$$), sum equals charge. $$K_2Cr_2O_7$$: Cr is $$+6$$; $$H_2SO_5$$: one peroxy O pair makes S $$+6$$.

nodes.label: Oxidising and Reducing Agents
nodes.note: Oxidiser gains electrons (is reduced); reducer loses electrons (is oxidised). $$KMnO_4, K_2Cr_2O_7, HNO_3$$ are common oxidisers; $$Zn, NaBH_4, H_2S$$ are common reducers. Disproportionation: same species oxidised and reduced, e.g. $$Cl_2 + 2NaOH \rightarrow NaCl + NaClO + H_2O$$.

nodes.label: Balancing Redox (Ion-Electron)
nodes.note: Split into half-reactions, balance atoms (O with $$H_2O$$, H with $$H^+$$ in acid), then electrons, then combine. Example: $$MnO_4^- + 5Fe^{2+} + 8H^+ \rightarrow Mn^{2+} + 5Fe^{3+} + 4H_2O$$.

nodes.label: Redox Titrations
nodes.note: Self-indicator titrations: $$MnO_4^-$$ (purple) vs oxalate or $$Fe^{2+}$$; endpoint is first permanent pink. Iodometric titration: $$I_2 + 2Na_2S_2O_3 \rightarrow 2NaI + Na_2S_4O_6$$ with starch blue-black endpoint.

nodes.label: Electrochemistry
nodes.note: Pillar chapter: Electrochemistry. Collects its JEE Main subtopics, trends and named tests in one branch.

nodes.label: Galvanic Cell and Daniell Cell
nodes.note: Spontaneous redox drives current: Daniell cell $$Zn|Zn^{2+}||Cu^{2+}|Cu$$, $$E^\circ_{cell} = 1.10$$ V, $$Zn$$ anode oxidised, $$Cu^{2+}$$ reduced at cathode. Salt bridge maintains electroneutrality.

nodes.label: Electrode Potential and Nernst Equation
nodes.note: Potential vs SHE (0.00 V). Nernst: $$E = E^\circ - \frac{0.0591}{n}\log Q$$ at 298 K. At equilibrium $$E = 0$$ and $$E^\circ = \frac{0.0591}{n}\log K$$. Connects EMF to $$\Delta G = -nFE$$.

nodes.label: Electrolytic Cell and Faraday's Laws
nodes.note: External EMF drives non-spontaneous reaction; products: cathode reduction, anode oxidation. Faraday: $$w = ZIt = \frac{M}{nF}It$$. Electrolysis of brine gives $$H_2$$, $$Cl_2$$ at cathode/anode; molten $$NaCl$$ gives Na and $$Cl_2$$.

nodes.label: Conductivity and Kohlrausch's Law
nodes.note: Molar conductivity $$\Lambda_m$$ rises on dilution for weak electrolytes; Debye-Huckel-Onsager: $$\Lambda_m = \Lambda_m^\circ - A\sqrt{c}$$. Kohlrausch: $$\Lambda_m^\circ = \lambda_+^\circ + \lambda_-^\circ$$; used to find $$K_a$$ of weak acids and $$K_{sp}$$ of sparingly soluble salts.

nodes.label: Batteries and Fuel Cells
nodes.note: Lead-acid (secondary): anode $$Pb + SO_4^{2-} \rightarrow PbSO_4 + 2e^-$$, cathode $$PbO_2 + SO_4^{2-} + 4H^+ + 2e^- \rightarrow PbSO_4 + 2H_2O$$, $$E \approx 2$$ V per cell. Fuel cell: $$2H_2 + O_2 \rightarrow 2H_2O$$, high efficiency ~75%.

nodes.label: Corrosion and Rusting
nodes.note: Rusting needs both $$O_2$$ and $$H_2O$$: anode $$Fe \rightarrow Fe^{2+} + 2e^-$$, cathode $$O_2 + 2H_2O + 4e^- \rightarrow 4OH^-$$; rust is $$Fe_2O_3 \cdot xH_2O$$. Prevention: galvanising (Zn), sacrificial Mg/Al, or coating.

nodes.label: Coordination Compounds
nodes.note: Pillar chapter: Coordination Compounds. Collects its JEE Main subtopics, trends and named tests in one branch.

nodes.label: Ligands and Denticity
nodes.note: Ligands donate lone pairs to the metal: unidentate ($$NH_3, H_2O, Cl^-, CO$$), bidentate ($$en, C_2O_4^{2-}$$), polydentate (EDTA, hexadentate). Ambidentate: $$NO_2^-$$ (N or O), $$SCN^-$$ (S or N). Chelates ring the metal and add stability (chelate effect).

nodes.label: Coordination Number and Oxidation State
nodes.note: In $$[Co(NH_3)_6]Cl_3$$: CN = 6, Co is $$+3$$. EAN = metal electrons + donated electrons, e.g. $$[Fe(CO)_5]$$: $$26 + 10 = 36$$ (Kr). Distinguishes coordination vs ionic sphere: ionisable Cl gives ppt with $$Ag^+$$.

nodes.label: IUPAC Nomenclature
nodes.note: Ligands named alphabetically (anionic end in -o: chloro, ammine for $$NH_3$$, aqua, carbonyl); metal oxidation state in Roman numerals; anionic complex gets -ate: $$K_4[Fe(CN)_6]$$ potassium hexacyanidoferrate(II).

nodes.label: Werner's Theory
nodes.note: Primary valency (ionisable, satisfied by anions outside sphere) and secondary valency (directed in space, inside sphere). $$CoCl_3 \cdot 6NH_3$$: all Cl inside, only 1 ionisable in $$[Co(NH_3)_5Cl]Cl_2$$-type? Classic series: $$[Co(NH_3)_6]Cl_3$$ (3 ionisable Cl), $$[Co(NH_3)_5Cl]Cl_2$$ (2), $$[Co(NH_3)_4Cl_2]Cl$$ (1).

nodes.label: Isomerism in Complexes
nodes.note: Structural: ionisation, hydrate, linkage ($$[Co(NH_3)_5(NO_2)]^{2+}$$ vs $$[Co(NH_3)_5(ONO)]^{2+}$$), coordination. Stereo: geometrical ($$cis/trans$$ in $$[Pt(NH_3)_2Cl_2]$$ - cisplatin is the $$cis$$ isomer) and optical ($$[Co(en)_3]^{3+}$$).

nodes.label: VBT for Complexes
nodes.note: Geometry from hybridisation: $$[NiCl_4]^{2-}$$ $$sp^3$$ tetrahedral paramagnetic; $$[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}$$ $$dsp^2$$ square planar diamagnetic. Octahedral: inner-orbital $$d^2sp^3$$ (strong field, e.g. $$[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}$$) vs outer-orbital $$sp^3d^2$$ (weak field).

nodes.label: Crystal Field Theory and CFSE
nodes.note: Ligands split d-orbitals: octahedral $$t_{2g}$$ (lower, 3 orbitals) and $$e_g$$ (higher, 2), gap $$\Delta_o$$; CFSE $$= (-0.4n_{t2g} + 0.6n_{eg})\Delta_o$$. Strong field gives low-spin (pairing), weak field high-spin.

nodes.label: Spectrochemical Series
nodes.note: Ligand field strength: $$I^- < Br^- < Cl^- < F^- < OH^- < H_2O < NH_3 < en < NO_2^- < CN^- < CO$$. Weak-field halides give high-spin coloured complexes; $$CN^-, CO$$ give low-spin, often colourless diamagnetic ones.

nodes.label: Jahn-Teller Distortion
nodes.note: Unequal occupancy of degenerate orbitals (e.g. $$d^9$$ $$Cu^{2+}$$, $$d^4$$ high-spin $$Mn^{3+}$$) distorts octahedron, usually elongating two axial bonds. Common in $$[Cu(H_2O)_6]^{2+}$$.

nodes.label: Stability Constants and EDTA
nodes.note: Stepwise stability constants $$K_1 > K_2 > ...$$; overall $$\beta_n = K_1K_2\cdots K_n$$. Chelation (EDTA, en) greatly increases stability (chelate effect). EDTA titrates $$Ca^{2+}/Mg^{2+}$$ in water hardness with Eriochrome Black T indicator: $$Ca^{2+} + Y^{4-} \rightarrow [CaY]^{2-}$$.

nodes.label: Isolation of Elements
nodes.note: Pillar chapter: Isolation of Elements. Collects its JEE Main subtopics, trends and named tests in one branch.

nodes.label: Principles of Metallurgy
nodes.note: Steps: concentration of ore, conversion to oxide, reduction, refining. Choice of reducing agent from Ellingham diagram ($$\Delta G$$ vs T): carbon reduces most oxides at high T, $$Al$$ reduces $$Cr_2O_3$$ (thermite).

nodes.label: Concentration of Ores
nodes.note: Froth flotation for sulfide ores ($$ZnS$$, $$PbS$$) with pine oil; magnetic separation for $$Fe_3O_4/MnO_2$$; leaching: bauxite $$Al_2O_3 \cdot 2H_2O$$ dissolved in $$NaOH$$ as $$NaAlO_2$$.

nodes.label: Extraction of Aluminium (Hall-Heroult)
nodes.note: Electrolysis of $$Al_2O_3$$ in molten cryolite $$Na_3AlF_6$$: cathode $$Al^{3+} + 3e^- \rightarrow Al$$, anode $$C + O^{2-} \rightarrow CO + 2e^-$$, overall $$2Al_2O_3 + 3C \rightarrow 4Al + 3CO_2$$.

nodes.label: Thermite Reaction
nodes.note: $$2Al + Fe_2O_3 \rightarrow Al_2O_3 + 2Fe$$, highly exothermic (~3000 K), used to weld railway rails. $$Mg$$ and $$Ca$$ similarly reduce $$TiCl_4$$ (Kroll process).

nodes.label: Extraction of Iron (Blast Furnace)
nodes.note: In a blast furnace, coke reduces haematite: $$C + O_2 \rightarrow CO_2$$, $$CO_2 + C \rightarrow 2CO$$, then $$Fe_2O_3 + 3CO \rightarrow 2Fe + 3CO_2$$. Limestone removes gangue: $$CaCO_3 \rightarrow CaO + CO_2$$, $$CaO + SiO_2 \rightarrow CaSiO_3$$.

nodes.label: Refining of Metals
nodes.note: Electrolytic refining (Cu, Ag, Au): impure anode, pure cathode in metal salt solution. Zone refining (Ge, Si) for semiconductors; Mond process for Ni: $$Ni + 4CO \xrightarrow{330K} Ni(CO)_4 \xrightarrow{450K} Ni + 4CO$$.

nodes.label: Mond Process for Nickel
nodes.note: Impure Ni heated with CO forms volatile $$Ni(CO)_4$$, which decomposes at 450 K to pure Ni. Basis of high-purity nickel production.

nodes.label: Qualitative Analysis (Salt Analysis)
nodes.note: Pillar chapter: Qualitative Analysis (Salt Analysis). Collects its JEE Main subtopics, trends and named tests in one branch.

nodes.label: Analysis of Cations (Groups 0-VI)
nodes.note: Systematic separation by selective precipitation using $$K_{sp}$$: Group 0 $$NH_4^+$$; I $$Ag^+, Pb^{2+}, Hg_2^{2+}$$ (dil HCl); II $$Cu^{2+}, Cd^{2+}, Bi^{3+}, Sn^{2+}, As^{3+}$$ ($$H_2S$$ in dil HCl); III $$Fe^{3+}, Al^{3+}, Cr^{3+}$$ ($$NH_4OH/NH_4Cl$$); IV $$Zn^{2+}, Mn^{2+}, Ni^{2+}, Co^{2+}$$ ($$H_2S$$ in basic); V $$Ba^{2+}, Sr^{2+}, Ca^{2+}$$ ($$(NH_4)_2CO_3$$); VI $$Mg^{2+}$$.

nodes.label: Group I: Ag+, Pb2+, Hg2^2+
nodes.note: Dil HCl precipitates white chlorides: $$AgCl, PbCl_2, Hg_2Cl_2$$. Hot water dissolves $$PbCl_2$$; $$NH_4OH$$ dissolves $$AgCl$$ as $$[Ag(NH_3)_2]^+$$ and blackens $$Hg_2Cl_2$$: $$Hg_2Cl_2 + 2NH_3 \rightarrow Hg + Hg(NH_2)Cl + NH_4Cl$$.

nodes.label: Group III: Fe3+, Al3+, Cr3+
nodes.note: $$NH_4OH$$ in presence of $$NH_4Cl$$ precipitates hydroxides: $$Fe(OH)_3$$ (red-brown), $$Al(OH)_3$$ (white gelatinous), $$Cr(OH)_3$$ (green). $$Fe^{3+}$$ confirmed by blood-red $$[Fe(SCN)]^{2+}$$ or Prussian blue with $$K_4[Fe(CN)_6]$$.

nodes.label: Group IV Confirmatory Tests
nodes.note: $$Ni^{2+}$$ gives rosy-red $$Ni(DMG)_2$$ with dimethylglyoxime; $$Co^{2+}$$ gives blue $$[Co(SCN)_4]^{2-}$$; $$Zn^{2+}$$ gives white $$ZnS$$/ash test (Rinmann's green $$CoO \cdot ZnO$$ with cobalt nitrate); $$Mn^{2+}$$ gives pink sulfide and purple $$MnO_4^-$$ with oxidiser.

nodes.label: Analysis of Anions (Classes A/B/C)
nodes.note: Class A (dil acid, gases): $$CO_3^{2-}, SO_3^{2-}, S^{2-}, NO_2^-, S_2O_3^{2-}, CH_3COO^-$$. Class B (conc $$H_2SO_4$$): $$Cl^-, Br^-, I^-, NO_3^-, C_2O_4^{2-}$$. Class C (precipitation): $$SO_4^{2-}, PO_4^{3-}, BO_3^{3-}$$. Soda extract $$Na_2CO_3$$ fusion makes salts water-soluble.

nodes.label: Brown Ring Test for Nitrate
nodes.note: $$NO_3^- + 3Fe^{2+} + 4H^+ \rightarrow 3Fe^{3+} + NO + 2H_2O$$; then $$Fe^{2+} + NO + 5H_2O \rightarrow [Fe(H_2O)_5(NO)]^{2+}$$ (brown ring at acid-water interface). Nitrite also gives a similar ring - destroy $$NO_2^-$$ with urea first.

nodes.label: Chromyl Chloride Test for Chloride
nodes.note: $$K_2Cr_2O_7 + 4NaCl + 6H_2SO_4 \rightarrow 2CrO_2Cl_2 + 2KHSO_4 + 4NaHSO_4 + 2H_2O$$; orange-red vapours ($$CrO_2Cl_2$$) turn NaOH yellow ($$Na_2CrO_4$$), and $$Ag^+$$ gives brown $$Ag_2CrO_4$$. Fails for $$AgCl, PbCl_2, HgCl_2$$.

nodes.label: Borax Bead Test
nodes.note: Heat borax $$Na_2B_4O_7 \cdot 10H_2O \rightarrow NaBO_2 + B_2O_3 + 10H_2O$$; the glassy bead dissolves metal oxides to coloured metaborates: Cu blue/green, Co blue, Cr green, Fe yellow/brown, Mn violet. A dry preliminary test for transition-metal cations.

nodes.label: Thenard's Blue and Rinmann's Green
nodes.note: Charcoal cavity + cobalt nitrate: $$Al^{3+}$$ gives Thenard's blue ($$CoO \cdot Al_2O_3$$), $$Zn^{2+}$$ gives Rinmann's green ($$CoO \cdot ZnO$$). Classic flame-colour-free dry tests in qualitative analysis.

nodes.label: Dry Heating and Flame Tests
nodes.note: Dry heating clues: blue/green $$Cu^{2+}$$ flame, $$ZnO$$ yellow when hot white when cold, decrepitation of $$Pb(NO_3)_2$$. Flame tests: Ca brick red, Sr crimson, Ba apple green, Na golden yellow, K lilac (viewed through cobalt glass).

nodes.label: Environmental Chemistry
nodes.note: Pillar chapter: Environmental Chemistry. Collects its JEE Main subtopics, trends and named tests in one branch.

nodes.label: Atmospheric Pollution
nodes.note: Key pollutants: $$CO$$ (carboxyhaemoglobin, reduces $$O_2$$ transport), $$SO_2$$ (acid rain precursor: $$SO_2 + H_2O \rightarrow H_2SO_3$$, oxidised to $$H_2SO_4$$), $$NO_x$$ (photochemical smog), particulates (PM2.5/PM10). Green chemistry aims to prevent waste at source.

nodes.label: Acid Rain
nodes.note: Rain with $$pH < 5.6$$ from $$SO_2, NO_x$$ oxidation: $$2SO_2 + O_2 + 2H_2O \rightarrow 2H_2SO_4$$, $$4NO_2 + O_2 + 2H_2O \rightarrow 4HNO_3$$. Damages marble ($$CaCO_3 + H_2SO_4$$) and acidifies lakes.

nodes.label: Greenhouse Gases and Global Warming
nodes.note: $$CO_2, CH_4, N_2O, CFCs$$ absorb outgoing IR, raising Earth's mean temperature. Methane is ~25x more potent than $$CO_2$$ over 100 years; rising from fossil fuels, rice paddies and landfills.

nodes.label: Ozone Layer and CFC Depletion
nodes.note: Stratospheric $$O_3$$ absorbs UV ($$O_3 \xrightarrow{h\nu} O_2 + O$$). CFCs ($$CFCl_3, CF_2Cl_2$$) photolyse to Cl radicals catalysing $$2O_3 \rightarrow 3O_2$$; Montreal Protocol phased CFCs out. More UV-B reaches surface, causing skin cancer risk.

nodes.label: Water Pollution and BOD
nodes.note: BOD (biochemical oxygen demand) measures organic load; high BOD depletes dissolved $$O_2$$, killing fish. Eutrophication from phosphates triggers algal blooms. Heavy metals $$Hg, Pb, Cd$$ bioaccumulate; Minamata disease from methyl-Hg.
